items.title: Attackers are using a SonicWall VPN flaw that skips SAML and MFA sign-in checks
items.why: SonicWall says a SonicOS SSL VPN bug lets someone with valid credentials for another login method bypass SAML and its MFA. CISA added it to its exploited list on November 6. Gen7 and Gen8 firewalls with SAML VPN login are exposed.
items.action: Upgrade SonicOS to 7.3.4-7013 (Gen7) or 8.2.3-8015 (Gen8) now; there is no workaround. Then review recent VPN logins for unfamiliar users.

items.title: QNAP says attackers are breaking into NAS devices through old Plex Media Server installs
items.why: New today: QNAP says some customers' NAS boxes were compromised through the Plex2Shell flaws in Plex Media Server, exploited since mid-October. QNAP's own operating system is not affected, but an exposed, unpatched Plex server puts the whole NAS at risk.
items.action: Update Plex to 1.43.3.10861 or later from the App Center and stop forwarding port 32400. If Plex was exposed while unpatched, reinstall QTS and reset Plex and NAS passwords.

items.title: OpenSSH fixes 'SSHole', which lets long passwords open locked accounts like root
items.why: On Linux systems built on musl without PAM, such as Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot and Yocto, any 257 to 1,024 character password can log in to accounts that should never accept one. No attacks yet, but it is simple to try.
items.action: Update to OpenSSH 10.6p2 and restart sshd on Alpine servers, containers and network gear; if you cannot patch yet, turn off SSH password logins.

items.title: DigiCert breach exposed business customer contacts and identity documents
items.why: A system that was left reachable from the internet after a 2025 migration was accessed from June 27. Names, business emails, phones and validation papers such as driver's licenses were taken. DigiCert says certificate issuance was not affected.
items.action: Treat unexpected emails or calls about your DigiCert certificates or this breach as suspect; verify through your DigiCert account, not links or numbers sent to you.

items.title: Fake OpenAI and SpaceX event invites hijack Microsoft 365 and Google work accounts
items.why: Researchers at Push found fake event sign-up pages aimed at marketing staff. Microsoft users get a device code that signs the attacker in, and Google users hit a proxy that captures passwords, MFA and session cookies.
items.action: Block Microsoft device-code sign-in with Conditional Access for anyone who does not need it, and tell staff never to enter a code from an event or invite page.

items.title: Veeam ships fixes for a critical Linux kernel flaw inside its backup appliances
items.why: New today: a 9.8-rated bug in Linux's TCP code affects Veeam Software and Infrastructure Appliances, Linux helpers and cloud plug-ins. Crash exploits are circulating, though no break-ins are confirmed. Backups are a top ransomware target.
items.action: Install the kernel update from Veeam Host Management and apply Veeam's private fix for Backup & Replication 13.1.2.57. On AMD EPYC hosts, watch the appliance reboot.
